newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks dragged down by Dow, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks dragged down by Dow, profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed down for the second day in a row as dealers took profits, spurred by a similar slide in Dow Industrials, traders said.
"The market was very dull. We thought it was going to close up, but the Dow dragged it down," said Francisco Blanco, equity research director at the Arka brokerage.

"However, it is noteworthy that the IPC did respect support at 3,320 points and may rebound to resistance at 3,380 points," he added. The blue chip IPC index closed 5.34 points down, or 0.16 percent, at 3,340.11.
The Dow Jones, meanwhile, closed 13.04 points off, or 0.22 percent, at 5,966.77.
Traders pointed out that profit-taking was only to be expected after the IPC had gained 4.3 percent last week.

"Some locals withheld stocks using the Indian Convention as an excuse, but the market was definitely dominated by profit-taking," a floor trader said. "Foreigners are still buying little and selecting issuers that concentrate on the domestic market." The National Indian Convention was due to start on Tuesday amid a huge controversy over whether or not rebel leaders from Chiapas should be allowed to attend.
Issuers deriving revenues mainly from the domestic market featured on the percentage gainers list, like paper company Kimber, housing firm Geo and food packagers Herdez.
On the broad market scoreboard, of 109 stocks that changed hands, losers outnumbered gainers by 50 to 37. Expectations
of primary rate falls did little to buttress the market, traders said, as they were forecast to be slight and had already been discounted.
A Reuters survey of 10 money market traders showed they expected the benchmark 28-day Cete rate to fall 22 basis points to an assignment rate of 22.84 percent.
